# AuthRight Harness

> Identity & Access Security Decision Layer for AI coding agents.

AuthRight Harness is the decision layer between your codebase and implementation. AI coding agents (Cursor, Codex, Claude Code) use AuthRight Harness to understand identity signals, record security decisions, and verify contracts before you hand work to coding agents via OpenSpec or Agent Plan-mode.

## Quick start

```bash
npm install -g @authright/cli@latest
authright --version
cd your-project
authright init --tools cursor,codex,claude
authright scan
```

Public loop: `scan` → pick `explore` or `change` → on that Auth Change record: `--analyze` → (explore: Agenda HITL | change: plan → `--set` → `--confirm-plan`) → `--ready` → `request-match` → `to-openspec` | `to-plan` → `review`. `doctor` is a peer command for findings, including before you pick explore or change — not a step between scan and that fork.

`/auth:explore` and `/auth:change` are two Decide commands — pick one. Explore is HITL recommend-and-choose; change is auto-plan. `/auth:to-openspec` and `/auth:to-plan` are two handoff commands — pick one. Product intent names use colon form (`/auth:scan`, `/auth:explore`, `/auth:change`, `/auth:request-match`, `/auth:to-openspec`, `/auth:to-plan`, `/auth:review`, `/auth:doctor`). Cursor registers hyphen slashes from the filename (`/auth-scan`); Claude Code registers colon slashes from `.claude/commands/auth/` (`/auth:scan`); Codex skills use `$authright-scan`. `authright init` prints the installed hosts’ forms.

AuthRight Harness does not write application source. It prepares accepted identity-security decisions for OpenSpec or Agent Plan-mode handoff (pick one).
